Body Characteristics: Fresh and elegant with gentle structure and fine perlage.
Finish Characteristics: Clean and refined with hints of ripe fruit and bread crust.
Aroma: Golden apple, white flowers, and subtle yeast notes.
Flavor: Crisp citrus, apple, and delicate pastry character.
Vinification: Traditional method with second fermentation in the bottle; Chardonnay grapes only.
Maturation: Aged for over 24 months on lees.
Type of cask: Stainless steel and bottle aging on lees
Color: Straw yellow with fine and persistent perlage.
General Recommended Accompanies: It pairs with all meals, perfect with fish and shellfish dishes. Excellent with vegetarian dishes full of sauces.
Stella Recommended: Gamberi All Aglio, Heirloom Burrata, Petrale Sole Piccata
Summary: Ferrari Brut is a flagship Trentodoc sparkling wine crafted entirely from Chardonnay grapes grown in the high-altitude vineyards of Trentino. Aged for over two years on the lees, it offers elegant aromas of apple and white flowers, vibrant acidity, and a refined mousse.
Unique Summary: One of Italy’s most iconic Metodo Classico sparkling wines, Ferrari Brut reflects the Alpine freshness and finesse of Trentino’s terroir.
Sustainability: Sustainably farmed hillside vineyards in Trentino; commitment to environmental stewardship and biodiversity.

Reviews.description: Enticing aromas of preserved lemon peel, ripe yellow apples and a whisper of honey leap from the glass. The palate is full and expressive, with Mandarin orangeinflected citrus tones taking center stage, supported by a creamy mousse and energetic acidity.

The NV Trentodoc Brut entices with a bouquet that mixes savory and sweet, with nuances of white peach and mint complicated by hints of crushed stone and an enriching note of brioche. It reverberates with zesty tension as crisp orchard fruits and sour citrus tones are elevated by juicy acidity. The Brut finishes with amazing length and complexity, leaving salty mineral tones offset by a twang of sour lime. The NV Brut punches well above its weight class.

A touch of nuttiness, offsetting scents of preserved lemon and pear. Redcurrant richness, creamy, rich and round, with impressive mousse and tangy red apple bite. Bubbles are well-formed and well-integrated, giving a creamy texture that melds into the richness of fruit. Sweet spices and nougat cream on the finish. Great stuff.

In the bottle with the white label, the Ferrari NV Trento Brut is a fresh and crisp Italian sparkler with the etched mineral notes of the Dolomites that add a special signature. The wine is lean and sharp, just what you need with finger foods on an aromatic terrace overlooking the sea. You can count on consistency with this well-priced production of three million bottles.

Wine Name: Brut Rosé, Faire La Fête, France
Body Characteristics: Refreshing and bright with a lively texture supported by tart citrus and green fruit.
Finish Characteristics: Crisp, lemony finish with lingering acidity and red fruit freshness.
Aroma: Golden apple, Bosc pear, red cherry, and white blossom.
Flavor: Green apple, tart citrus peel, red cherry, and floral notes.
Vinification: Méthode traditionnelle; aged sur lie in bottle for 15–18 months with a dosage of 7 g/L.
Color: Rosé with bright, pale pink hue and fine bubbles.
General Recommended Accompanies: Seafood, fried appetizers, sautéed dishes, or enjoyed on its own.
Summary: Faire La Fête Brut Rosé is a méthode traditionnelle sparkling wine from Limoux, combining Chardonnay, Chenin Blanc, and Pinot Noir. With notes of red cherry, citrus peel, and floral lift, it's bright, refreshing, and ideal for celebrations or casual sipping.
Unique Summary: A French sparkling rosé aged 15+ months on lees, delivering tart citrus and floral freshness at exceptional value.

Reviews.description: With 60% Chardonnay, 25% Chenin Blanc, and 15% Pinot Noir, this fine value mingles scents of baguette, strawberry, salty lime, and red apple with crisp acidity and flavors of more strawberry and ruby grapefruit, which lead to touches of grassy herb and white pepper.

COMMENTARY: The Faire la Fête Crémant de Limoux Brut Rosé is enticing and beautiful. TASTING NOTES: This wine exhibits attractive aromas and flavors of ripe strawberries and spicy earth. Enjoy its soft yet balance style with a plate of mix sushi. (Tasted: April 4, 2020, San Francisco, CA)

Wine Name: Champagne, Perrier-Jouët, Grand Brut, Epernay, NV
Body Characteristics: Elegant, complex, crisp and balanced with a fine, persistent mouthfeel.
Finish Characteristics: Lingering flavors of fresh apples and lemons.
Aroma: Tropical fruit, citrus, spice, and yeast.
Flavor: Fresh apples, lemons, crisp citrus, and subtle brioche notes.
Vinification: Fermented in modern, temperature-controlled stainless steel tanks. Wines are selected from over 300 lots, blended with 20% reserve wine.
Maturation: Aged in historic chalk cellars located 50 feet underground at a constant temperature of 52°F.
Type of cask: Stainless steel, then bottle-aged in chalk cellars
Vineyard: Sourced from 35–40 crus; includes grapes from Cramant and Côte des Blancs
Stella Recommended: Fish of the Day, Risotto, Seafood
Summary: Perrier-Jouët Grand Brut NV is a refined Champagne made from a blend of Pinot Noir, Pinot Meunier, and Chardonnay. Crafted from up to 40 crus and aged in chalk cellars, it delivers a golden hue with tropical fruit and citrus aromas, crisp acidity, and a persistent, elegant finish.
Unique Summary: Crafted from 40 crus and aged in Champagne's historic chalk cellars, this wine blends elegance and complexity with fresh citrus and apple-driven vibrancy.

Reviews.description: Oyster shell, smoke and fleur de sel aromas lead on the nose of this mouthwatering Champagne, while the plush, creamy mousse carries flavors of poached quince, tangerine sorbet, candied ginger and brioche. Long and minerally on the well-cut and re- freshing finish. Pinot Noir, Meunier and Chardonnay.
A silky Champagne with aromas of apricot pie, shortcrust, croissants, lemon curd and seashells. Very fine, soft bubbles. Gentle salinity underneath the pastry notes, with a soft finish. Drink now.

Body Characteristics: Light-bodied with a delicate mousse and refreshing, easy-drinking texture.
Finish Characteristics: Clean and aromatic with lingering floral and fruit notes.
Aroma: Intense aromas of citrus, apricot, fig, and orange blossom.
Flavor: Pleasantly sweet with citrus, apricot, fig, and floral notes mirroring fresh Moscato grapes.
Vinification: Manually harvested grapes are softly pressed and naturally clarified. Fermentation occurs in pressurized vats and is stopped through filtration at 5% alcohol to preserve natural sweetness and delicate bubbles.
Maturation: No extended aging; bottled early to preserve freshness and aromatics.
General Recommended Accompanies: Desserts, panna cotta, appetizers, raw fish, sushi
Summary: A lightly sparkling Moscato d’Asti from Strevi showcasing bright citrus, apricot, and orange blossom aromas. Crafted with early-stopped fermentation, it delivers a naturally low-alcohol, sweet, and refreshing profile with delicate bubbles. A perfect dessert or aperitif wine with vibrant aromatics.
Unique Summary: A naturally sweet, low-alcohol Moscato with delicate bubbles and vibrant floral aromatics from a prized Strevi cru.

Reviews.description: This savory, lightly sparkling dessert wine has intense aromas of ripe yellow peach, sage and orange blossom. The aromas carry over to the tangy, foaming palate along with blood orange and lemon drop candy. Vibrant acidity and energizing mineral notes keep it fresh and balanced. — Kerin O’Keefe
Bright straw yellow. Banana and yellow peach on the nose, with a hint of thyme on the finish. Smooth notion on the palate, accessible and uncomplicated, shows yellow fruit and good balance.

Body Characteristics: Crisp, easy to drink with a soft finish and harmonious citrus character.
Finish Characteristics: Soft finish with bright citrus lingering.
Flavor: Bright citrus fruits, crisp apple, subtle florals.
Vinification: Fermented at controlled temperatures (16–18°C), aged naturally on lees for structure, then undergoes second fermentation in autoclave (Charmat Method).
Maturation: Lees aging followed by autoclave rest before bottling.
General Recommended Accompanies: Dishes with a delicate flavour, such as light appetizers or fish-based dishes
Summary: Val D’Oca Prosecco Treviso Extra Dry is a refreshing and crisp sparkling wine from Veneto, crafted primarily from Glera. Its fragrant nose of apple and wildflowers pairs with bright citrus flavors and a soft, smooth finish.
Unique Summary: Produced using the Charmat method, this Prosecco balances floral aromas and citrusy vibrancy with a soft, approachable finish.

Blend: 81% Pinot Noir, 11% Petite Sirah, 6% Muscat Canelli, 2% Moscato Giallo
Body Characteristics: Light, lively structure with refreshing weight and bright fruit-driven profile.
Finish Characteristics: Clean and crisp with lingering watermelon, peach, and citrus notes.
Aroma: Candied peach, watermelon, blood orange, and bright fresh fruit aromas.
Flavor: Pink starburst candy, peach, watermelon, and blood orange with vibrant fruit intensity.
Vinification: Whole cluster pressed with minimal skin contact. Components fermented separately for approximately 14 days at cool temperatures in stainless steel tanks.
Maturation: Short maturation to preserve freshness and fruit purity.
Vineyard: Russian River Valley and Guenoc vineyards with additional Sonoma County selections.
Summary: The Banshee Rosé 2023 from Sonoma County showcases vibrant acidity and playful fruit character developed during a cooler growing season. Crafted primarily from Pinot Noir, the wine bursts with watermelon, peach, and blood orange flavors layered with nostalgic pink candy notes. Fermented in stainless steel to preserve freshness, this rosé is crisp, lively, and refreshing, ideal for warm weather enjoyment.
Unique Summary: A playful Sonoma rosé bursting with pink candy, watermelon, and citrus brightness driven by cool-climate acidity.

Reviews.description: Juicy and compelling in fresh berry fruit, this wine offers light baking spice and dried herb components that balance it and provide complexity. Crisp and light in style, it's ready for summertime sipping.

COMMENTARY: The Banshee Rosé is one of my favorites in the marketplace, and the 2018 vintage is true to excellent self. TASTING NOTES: This wine is delicious and nicely balanced, with a bit of perkiness in the finish. Its aromas and flavors of ripe raspberry and an accent of minerality should pair it nicely with cashew chicken accented by a touch of chili oil. (Tasted: March 8, 2019, San Francisco, CA)
